facts.statement: The IFSCA Payment Services Regulations, 2024 were notified on 29 January 2024 and amended on 2 April 2024 to expand the escrow definition to 'one or more parties'; the legal form for a payment service provider is a company only (not LLP or branch).
The five regulated payment services (Schedule I Part A) are: account issuance, e-money issuance, escrow, cross-border money transfer, and merchant acquisition.

Excluded activities (Schedule I Part B): agent-negotiated transactions, cheque/draft/traveller's cheque instruments, inter-PSP settlement system transactions, intra-group transactions, currency transport, technical service providers not possessing funds, and limited-use payment instruments.

A Significant PSP is one whose monthly average transaction value exceeds USD 2 million for a single service or USD 4 million for two or more services, or whose e-money daily average stored value exceeds USD 3 million, or whose e-money issuance daily average exceeds USD 3 million.

PSP net worth requirements: Regular PSP USD 100,000 rising to USD 200,000 within 3 years; Significant PSP USD 250,000 rising to USD 500,000 within 3 years; a single authorisation covers all payment services.
facts.detail: Additional net worth under Schedule V must be met within 180 days of communication; security deposit is released 1 year after surrender/revocation approval.

facts.statement: PSPs must maintain separate escrow accounts per payment service with an IBU; Schedule II fit-and-proper criteria list 10 disqualifications with a 3-year lookback for debarment-type orders.

Under the draft PS Regulations 2023, a refused applicant could make a fresh application after 6 months, and security deposits were USD 100,000 (monthly transaction value up to USD 6 million) or USD 200,000 (above USD 6 million).

The IFSCA (Payments Regulatory Board) Regulations, 2025 were notified on 12 September 2025, replacing the earlier Board for Payment and Settlement Systems (BPSS) framework; FCSS bye-laws were notified 3 October 2025 with FCSS instructions for IBUs on 7 October 2025.
facts.detail: FCSS is being set up by a CCIL subsidiary.
